title: Rig Project config (rig.yaml)
description: Committed Project intent: identity, Services, Tools, routes and Target patches.

production_branch.description: Branch whose pushes deploy the Stable Target; defaults to the Host deploy.production_branch, then main.

domain.description: Stable Target hostname. Previews default to <preview-name>.<domain>; the Working copy has no hostname unless its patch sets one. ${rig.target} is the only reference a hostname may contain.

supervisor.description: Process supervisor: rigd (child processes owned by the daemon) or launchd (per-Service launchd agents). The Project sets it for all its Services. It can also be set per Target role under targets.<role>.supervisor.

build.description: Shared shell build command, run once in the workspace before any Service or Tool build. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.ready_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}. A Service's env is not available here.

build_timeout.description: Duration budget for the shared build and the default for Service and Tool builds (default 10m).

env.description: Public environment values passed to the process; never put secrets here. Values may use ${...} references. Bind-style keys such as HOST or BIND_ADDR may not use a wildcard address.

additionalProperties.description: Public value. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.ready_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

env_file.description: Environment file path, or an ordered list of paths where later files win. Listed files are required and hold plain KEY=value data; their contents never take part in ${...} references. Relative paths resolve against the workspace; ~ is the operator home. The path itself may use references. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.ready_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

propertyNames.description: Service or Tool name used in references, dependencies and output.

run.description: Foreground shell command run with /bin/sh -c; explicit bindings must be localhost only. Referenced values with spaces or shell characters are single-quoted unless the reference is already quoted. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.ready_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

build.description: Shell build command of this Service, run with /bin/sh -c in the workspace during preparation, never as a start hook; explicit bindings must be localhost only. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.ready_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

build_timeout.description: Build duration budget such as 10m; a build past it is terminated and recorded as failed, never as completed.

ports.description: Named local TCP ports: auto lets Rig choose and keep a free port, a number from 1 to 65535 pins it. Previews always use chosen ports.

ready.description: Local HTTP URL or shell command used to check readiness; referenced values in a shell command are quoted as in run. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.ready_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

ready_timeout.description: Startup readiness budget such as 30s (the default).

depends_on.description: Services that must be running and ready before this one starts; a later dependency failure does not restart this Service.

items.description: Service or Tool name used in references, dependencies and output.

restart.description: Automatic restart after a known exit: always (default), on-failure, or no. An explicit up or restart starts the Service under every policy.
